_comment: A7/C6. Deny-by-default egress with an allowlist. Enforcement is nftables default-drop
OUTSIDE the container; this file is the declaration and the canary below is the
verification. The split matters: environment-variable proxy configuration is advisory
and bypassable, so a policy asserted by reading configuration asserts nothing.
The canary targets are IP literals AND a DNS name, deliberately. An IP literal tests
raw egress with DNS removed as a confound; a DNS name tests resolution. A canary that
only ever fails at name resolution proves nothing about egress on a host with no
resolver — it would report the same green on a correctly firewalled container and on a
container whose /etc/resolv.conf is empty while every port is open.
forbidden_allowlist_patterns: C6 also requires that no package registry appears in the
allowlist. The runtime image is pulled OUTSIDE the sandbox network namespace precisely
so no registry needs to be reachable from inside, and a registry host here would undo
that without touching any other control.

canary_targets.reason: Raw egress with DNS removed as a confound. A public resolver's TLS port, chosen because it is reachable from any unfiltered network and belongs to nobody this project transacts with.
Name resolution plus egress. Also the single most consequential host to be able to reach from inside the sandbox: it is how a denied distribution would arrive.
